purpose: Determine whether the unresolved credit_supply_capacity node can be mapped directly into the observed ECB BSI credit-flow reference mode without conflating bank supply conditions, borrower demand and realized financial transactions.

ecb_bls.source: Bank Lending Survey methodology and releases
ecb_bls.finding: The BLS complements loan statistics with separate information on loan supply and loan demand. Credit standards measure banks' approval policies; loan demand is independently surveyed.
ecb_bls.interpretation: Realized loan developments reflect interactions between supply conditions and financing demand, so a realized transaction flow does not identify a supply-capacity state by itself.

ecb_bls_forecasting_evidence.source: Economic Bulletin analysis of BLS information and future loan developments
ecb_bls_forecasting_evidence.finding: Credit standards and loan demand each provide information for actual loan growth, and combining supply and demand information can improve forecasts.

retained_credit_flow_reference.concept: ECB BSI financial transactions for domestic NFC and household/NPISH loans, MFIs excluding the NCB, all currencies combined.

retained_aggregate_credit_review.finding: The current aggregate reduced form mixes credit demand and credit supply; realized BLS credit standards and loan demand must remain separate observables.

structural_interpretation.credit_supply_capacity_role: Unresolved supply-side umbrella over standards, risk tolerance, prudential/funding constraints and willingness/ability to lend.
structural_interpretation.credit_flow_role: Observed realized financial transaction on the ECB BSI private non-financial loan boundary.
structural_interpretation.demand_role: Borrower financing demand is a separate determinant of realized lending and must not be inferred from the realized flow alone.
structural_interpretation.future_identification_requirement: Any quantitative supply-to-flow equation requires a preregistered sector-specific design with separate realized supply-condition and demand observables, matched lending-rate/activity controls and an untouched evaluation/identification gate.
